To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
allergic disease–produced nitric oxide suppresses the hepatic flavin-containing monooxygenase 1 and flavin-containing monoxgenase 3 enzymes.

the hepatic micrososomal flavin-containing monooxygenase 1 (FMO1) and 3 (FMO3) activities were suppressed by type 1 allergic diseases, which were associated with increased levels of serum nitric oxide (a product of inducible nitric oxide synthase).
type 1 allergy-produced NO suppressed the FMO3 activity of BDZ, which was restored by the addition of ascorbate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of allergy-induced NO on FMO1 and 3 activities.
the pharmacokinetic implications of FMOs for drug metabolism in patients with type 1 allergy.
the effects of NO produced by type 1 allergy on the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of drugs metabolized mainly by FMO3 in humans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the suppression of FMOs by NO is an interesting and novel aspect of the interaction of NO with drug-metabolizing enzymes.
the suppression of FMO1/3 metabolism is related to the reversible S-nitroso modification of iNOS derived NO.
the suppression of BDN N-oxygenation by NO is probably due to the reversible modification of FMO3 by NO.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FMO3 activity is suppressed by NO, which may affect the pharmacokinetic properties of FMO3-dependent drugs.
type 1 allergic disease produced NO that suppressed FMO3 metabolism.
the type 1 allergy-induced NO suppressed FMO3 activity through reversible S-nitroso modification of iNOS, which was not observed in FMO1-dependent imipramine N-oxidation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the allergic response can alter FMO activity and that this can be a significant source of variability for drug disposition.
allergic NO suppressed the hepatic FMO3 activity, which may affect drug metabolism in allergic individuals.
allergic NO suppressed hepatic micrososomal FMO3-dependent N-oxidation of BDZ in type 1 allergy.
